The failing test `testCalendarTimezoneRespected` in `FastDateFormat_PrinterTest` creates a `Calendar` instance with a specific timezone (`anotherZone`), formats the current time in this timezone using `SimpleDateFormat`, and then tries to format the same time using `FastDateFormat`. The test expects the same result from both formatters when formatting the time in the specified timezone.

The bug report mentions that the `FastDateFormat`'s "z" pattern does not respect the timezone of `Calendar` instances passed to format. Looking at the `FastDateFormat.format(Date)` method, it simply delegates the formatting to a `Printer` instance without considering the timezone.

Therefore, it seems that the issue lies in the implementation of the `Printer` used by `FastDateFormat`, which does not take into account the timezone information passed from `Calendar`.

Next, I will retrieve the code snippet of the `Printer` implementation to further investigate the bug.
